messages.text: Penalised Antonelli to help Russell at Italian GP

metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli is ready to help Mercedes team-mate and title rival George Russell in qualifying at the Italian Grand Prix for a race the world championship leader will start at the back of the grid due to an engine penalty.
metadata.content: Italian GP: Kimi Antonelli to help Mercedes team-mate George Russell in Monza qualifying due to engine grid penalty | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Italian GP: Kimi Antonelli to help Mercedes team-mate George Russell in Monza qualifying due to engine grid penalty Back-of-the-grid start for Kimi Antonelli at Monza means title leader open to helping George Russell's bid for pole in Q3 on Saturday; watch Friday's practice sessions for the Italian GP at 11.30am and 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Thursday 3 September 2026 17:31, UK Image: George Russell is looking to claw back some of his 59-point championship deficit to Kimi Antonelli this weekend Kimi Antonelli is ready to help Mercedes team-mate and title rival George Russell in qualifying at the Italian Grand Prix for a race the world championship leader will start at the back of the grid due to an engine penalty. Italy's own Antonelli arrives at his home track of Monza knowing that his healthy points advantage is almost certain to be eaten into this weekend owing to the fact Mercedes are triggering a back-of-the-grid start for him by exceeding power-unit component limits on his car, a legacy of reliability issues from earlier in the season. Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton both trail Antonelli by 59 points while McLaren's Lando Norris, the winner of the last two races, is 83 points behind. messages.text: Antonelli: Ferrari an incredible brand but I’m happy at Mercedes

metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli played down suggestions that he could drive for Ferrari in the future as he claimed he could spend his entire career with Mercedes.
metadata.content: Kimi Antonelli: Mercedes driver plays down speculation around future switch to Ferrari ahead of Italian GP | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Kimi Antonelli: Mercedes driver plays down speculation around future switch to Ferrari ahead of Italian GP Kimi Antonelli goes into his home race at the top of the Drivers' Championship; the Italian responded to speculation that he could drive for Ferrari later in his career; watch Friday's practice sessions for the Italian GP at 11.30am and 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Thursday 3 September 2026 17:10, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli says he understands the likely long-running speculation that Ferrari will make a move for him in the future, but insists he 'still has a lot to give back' at Mercedes. Kimi Antonelli played down suggestions that he could drive for Ferrari in the future as he claimed he could spend his entire career with Mercedes. The 20-year-old Italian has exceeded all expectations to lead the Drivers' Championship by 59 points after 12 rounds of just his second season in Formula 1. Antonelli's superb 2026 form has seen his popularity grow massively in Italy, creating a potential dilemma for the home fans at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix who would usually be loyal to Ferrari. messages.text: Hamilton reveals hope of becoming first black Ferrari driver to win in Italy

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton says he has been considering the magnitude of potentially becoming the first black Ferrari Formula 1 driver to win a home race for the team, ahead of this weekend's Italian Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton shares thoughts about possibility of becoming first black Ferrari driver to win in Italy ahead of Italian GP | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Lewis Hamilton shares thoughts about possibility of becoming first black Ferrari driver to win in Italy ahead of Italian GP Lewis Hamilton is seeking his first Ferrari victory in Italy this weekend in Monza; Hamilton is hopeful a Ferrari engine upgrade will boost his chances; watch Friday's practice sessions for the Italian GP at 11.30am and 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Thursday 3 September 2026 16:07, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton arrived at the Italian GP in a rare Ferrari F40 and revealed that the car's engine bore the same number as his racing number. Lewis Hamilton says he has been considering the magnitude of potentially becoming the first black Ferrari Formula 1 driver to win a home race for the team, ahead of this weekend's Italian Grand Prix. The seven-time world champion has enjoyed a much improved second campaign in red, with a maiden Grand Prix victory for the team in Barcelona in June helping to keep him in title contention, as he trails Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli by 59 points with 11 rounds remaining. Hamilton's hopes of claiming victory in Monza have been boosted by the fact Antonelli will start from the back of the grid as he serves a penalty for exceeding his engine-part allowance. metadata.content: Arsenal vs Chelsea: Does Xabi Alonso have a style issue? And will it affect ability to compete at top of Premier League? | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Arsenal vs Chelsea: Does Xabi Alonso have a style issue? And will it affect ability to compete at top of Premier League? The standout fixture of this weekend sees champions Arsenal host Chelsea in a match between two of the four teams on maximum points; Arsenal are yet to concede a goal, while Chelsea are the joint top scorers; watch Arsenal vs Chelsea live on Sky Sports on Sunday Laura Hunter Football Features Writer Thursday 3 September 2026 17:39, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Carragher said he was not expecting Xabi Alonso's new style of football since arriving at Chelsea. Much of the last week in the Premier League has bordered on the ridiculous. Spending in the transfer window went stratospheric. Total expenditure topped £3.4bn by Deadline Day's close. Chelsea's outlay of £340m on 13 players was the second highest of any side. But their performances across the opening weeks of the campaign have turned heads, too. At a practical level, Chelsea's squad looks as balanced as it ever has during the Todd Boehly era, with a pivot towards recruiting experience over raw potential.
